brief.topic: A Little Darkness Makes a Picture

s01: Inside a dark box, a candle appears upside down.
A tiny opening has sorted the light.
We are looking at a simplified side view.
Light from the top of the candle travels straight through the opening.
It reaches the lower part of the screen.
Light from the bottom reaches the upper part.
The crossing happens at the hole.
No lens needs to turn the light around.
Only a narrow set of rays from each point gets through.
The two triangles have the same shape.
Image height divided by object height equals screen distance divided by object distance.
Move the screen farther from the hole, and the image grows.
Keep that screen still and move the candle farther away.
Real openings also trade brightness against blur and diffraction.
Here we are following the ideal straight rays.
A little darkness lets one arrangement of light become a picture.

scenes.narration:
Inside a dark box, a candle appears upside down. A tiny opening has sorted the light.

We are looking at a simplified side view. Light from the top of the candle travels straight through the opening. It reaches the lower part of the screen. Light from the bottom reaches the upper part.

The crossing happens at the hole. No lens needs to turn the light around. Only a narrow set of rays from each point gets through.

The two triangles have the same shape. Image height divided by object height equals screen distance divided by object distance. Move the screen farther from the hole, and the image grows.

Keep that screen still and move the candle farther away. Now its image becomes smaller. Real openings also trade brightness against blur and diffraction. Here we are following the ideal straight rays. A little darkness lets one arrangement of light become a picture.
